Reference Fact: Patient presented with progressive exertional breathlessness.
Patient was hypoxic at presentation, with SpO2 89% on room air.
Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) was diagnosed.
CT pulmonary angiography confirmed chronic thromboembolic disease.
Echocardiography demonstrated severe pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular strain.
V/Q scanning demonstrated mismatched perfusion defects consistent with CTEPH.
NT-proBNP was markedly elevated during the clinical course.
Supplemental low-flow oxygen therapy was used to treat hypoxia.
Therapeutic anticoagulation was initiated during the clinical course.
Rivaroxaban was used for ongoing/long-term anticoagulation.
Furosemide was used during management of pulmonary hypertension/right-heart strain and fluid retention.
Sildenafil 20 mg three times daily was introduced for pulmonary hypertension management.
Physiotherapy included breathing exercises and progressive mobilisation.
Energy-conservation/pacing strategies and a home exercise programme were provided.
Mild anaemia was documented later in the course and treated with ferrous sulfate.
Breathlessness and exercise tolerance improved during the clinical course.
Supplemental oxygen requirements decreased, with the patient later maintaining approximately 94-95% SpO2 on room air.
The patient was referred to a tertiary pulmonary hypertension centre for pulmonary endarterectomy assessment.
The patient was ultimately discharged after clinical improvement.
Follow-up at the tertiary pulmonary hypertension centre was planned after discharge.
